claims.text: No GitHub or GitLab credential lives in plugin configuration: every forge component authenticates through the gh/glab CLI login store or a process environment token (GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN/GITLAB_TOKEN); the config schema for github/gitlab accepts only `remote`.

Only the protected-branch read (scripts/protected-lookup.py -> adapters/forge/branch_protection.py) chooses the host per repository: host from the branch's remote URL, `--hostname <host>` only when the CLI hosts file lists it, an error rather than a default-host read otherwise.

The forge adapters never pass a host: `github.remote`/`gitlab.remote` reduce the remote URL to owner/name with the host stripped (project_from_remote.py), and every `gh api`/`glab api` call carries no --hostname.

Inference: on a non-default host (GitHub Enterprise, self-hosted GitLab) with `<kind>.remote` set, `gh --repo owner/name` and every `gh api repos/...` go to gh's default host, and GitLab `glab api projects/:id` follows the cwd remote while `glab mr -R` names a host-less path; the adapters can address the wrong host. Rests on gh/glab resolution rules, which are external and not checked here.

Two repositories on one machine can use different hosts today only through the CLIs' own per-host logins and each checkout's git remote; the protection read handles this per repository, the forge adapters only when `<kind>.remote` is unset and the CLI derives the host from the checkout (inferred for the adapters).

Two repositories on the same host cannot use different accounts through any plugin mechanism: no config key, no per-repository token and no account switch exists; the only levers are process-wide (GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN/GITLAB_TOKEN in the session environment, or GH_CONFIG_DIR/GLAB_CONFIG_DIR, which the plugin reads only to find logged-in hosts). An SSH host alias such as `github.com-work` is resolved back to github.com by the protection read, which then uses the default account.

GitHub Issues tracker and report-issue target github.com owner/name with no host: github-issues uses `--repo <github-issues.repo or GH_REPO>`; report-issue strips a github.com prefix and passes -R owner/name.

Tests pin the protection read's token order, host flag and SSH alias handling; no test pins the forge adapters' `<kind>.remote` -> --repo/-R path, the host-less `gh api` calls, or `auth-status` identity on a non-default host (unguarded).
PROVIDERS.md § Credentials documents Jira only; no document states the GitHub/GitLab host or account rule, and no document the code refutes was found.

Account identity is per host and per machine: gh/glab hold one active login per host in their config store, and the plugin never selects an account; `auth-status`, `forge_user` and the ledger's trusted-author identity (`_identity`, `reconstruct_state`, `_trusted_set`) all read `api user` with no host flag.

The protection read has four entry points, each reading GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN/GITLAB_TOKEN from its own process environment: the PreToolUse guard (hooks/hooks.json:73), the pre-commit and reference-transaction git hooks through hooks/git-backstop.py:35 and :71-81 (hooks/precommit-gates.sh:47, hooks/branch-name-gate.sh:54, :68), and scripts/afk-launch.py:32.

claims.text: The plugin-shipped tracker registrations (.mcp.json, .mcp.codex.json) carry no env block, so that server resolves Jira credentials from the harness env and then the file walk.

Two repositories can use different Jira accounts only on the MCP tool path, when each repository has its own tracker registration whose env the harness passes into the server process (env outranks files); the publishing scripts run without that env and resolve one set per machine, and the walk can hand repository A's project-scoped block to a script run in repository B.
Forge verbs pass --repo/-R as owner/name with the remote host stripped, so gh/glab pick the host; only the branch-protection read passes --hostname derived from the remote host.
The Codex credential reader hardcodes ~/.codex/config.toml and ignores CODEX_HOME, which setup's other Codex config reader honours.

The forge protection read takes the host from the repository's own remote and calls the CLI with --hostname for that host; the account is the CLI's stored login for that host, so the host is per repository and the account is per host per machine
Two repositories on one host share one CLI account: an SSH alias that resolves to github.com gets no --hostname and uses the single github.com login
